examples.ko: 과학 시간에 바닷물을 증류해서 소금을 분리했어요.
examples.en: In science class, we distilled seawater to separate out the salt.
If you distill water, the impurities are removed.

examples.ko: 이 기계는 해수를 증류해 마실 물을 만들어요.
examples.en: This machine distills seawater to make drinking water.

examples.ko: 먼저 액체를 끓인 다음 증기를 식혀서 증류해요.
examples.en: First you boil the liquid, then cool the steam to distill it.
I learned how to distill through an experiment.
They distill roses to make rose water.

explain: 그냥 '끓이다'와 달리, 끓어서 나온 증기를 다시 식혀 액체로 받아 내는 과정까지 포함해요. '증류수'라는 말이 일상에서 가장 흔하고, 동사는 과학 수업이나 설명에서 주로 써요.

phrases.en: I distilled seawater and got clean water.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어서'로 이어서 증류한 다음에 일어난 결과를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-아/어서' ending links distilling to the result that follows.

phrases.example: 실험할 때는 수돗물 대신 증류수를 써요.
phrases.en: In experiments, we use distilled water instead of tap water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사 '증류하다'에서 나온 말로, 증류해서 만든 물이에요. 일상에서 가장 흔하게 들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun from the verb, meaning water made by distilling. It is the most common form in daily life.

phrases.example: 물을 증류하는 방법을 과학 시간에 배웠어요.
phrases.en: We learned how to distill water in science class.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는 방법'을 붙여 과정이나 방법을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-는 방법' lets you talk about the method or process.

explain_en: Unlike plain '끓이다' (to boil), it includes the step of cooling the steam and collecting it as a liquid again. The noun '증류수' (distilled water) is the most common form in daily life, while the verb is mainly used in science classes and explanations.

examples.en: My grandmother in the countryside sent me native honey.
Native honey is more expensive than regular honey.

examples.ko: 감기에 걸렸을 때 토종꿀을 따뜻한 물에 타 마셔요.
examples.en: When I have a cold, I mix native honey into warm water and drink it.

examples.ko: 이 토종꿀은 맛이 진하고 향이 좋아요.
examples.en: This native honey has a rich taste and a nice scent.
They say it's native honey collected directly in the mountains.
I bought a jar of native honey as a gift.

explain: '토종'은 그 땅에서 오래 자란 원래 품종이라는 뜻이라 '토종꿀'은 한국 토종벌이 만든 꿀을 말해요. 보통 양봉 꿀보다 귀하고 비싸다고 생각해서 선물로도 많이 줘요. 반대로 외국에서 들어온 종류는 '외래종'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I received a jar of native honey as a gift.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꿀은 병에 담아 팔아서 '한 병'으로 세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Honey is sold in jars, so it is counted as '한 병'.

phrases.en: I gave my parents native honey as a present.
phrases.nuance_ko: 귀한 꿀이라 선물로 많이 주고받아요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is valued, so it is often given as a gift.
phrases.en_equiv: to give native honey as a gift

phrases.en: It's rarer because it's honey made by native bees.
phrases.nuance_ko: '토종꿀'을 만드는 한국 원래의 벌을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The native Korean bee that makes '토종꿀'.

explain_en: '토종' refers to an original breed long native to the land, so '토종꿀' is honey made by native Korean bees. It is generally seen as rarer and pricier than farmed honey and is often given as a gift. The opposite, a species brought from abroad, is '외래종'.

examples.ko: 침 속에는 음식을 소화시키는 효소가 있어요.
examples.en: Saliva contains enzymes that digest food.

examples.ko: 요즘 효소 음료가 건강에 좋다고 인기예요.
examples.en: Enzyme drinks are popular these days as good for health.
We learned the role of enzymes in science class.

examples.ko: 파인애플에는 고기를 부드럽게 하는 효소가 들어 있어요.
examples.en: Pineapple has an enzyme that tenderizes meat.

examples.ko: 효소는 온도가 너무 높으면 일을 못 해요.
examples.en: Enzymes cannot work when the temperature is too high.
My grandmother makes plum enzyme syrup by herself.

explain: 과학 시간에 나오는 단어지만 한국에서는 '매실 효소', '곡물 효소'처럼 과일이나 곡물을 설탕에 재워 만든 건강 음료나 식품 이름으로도 자주 써요. 앞에 오는 말과 함께 '소화 효소'처럼 쓰는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: If you lack digestive enzymes, your stomach feels uncomfortable.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식을 소화시키는 효소를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to enzymes that digest food.

phrases.en: My mom made plum enzyme syrup.
phrases.nuance_ko: 매실을 설탕에 재워 만든 음료나 식품 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A drink made by steeping plums in sugar.

phrases.en: I drink an enzyme drink in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 효소가 들어 있어 건강에 좋다고 하는 음료를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A drink said to be healthy because it contains enzymes.

explain_en: A science-class word, but in Korea it is also commonly used for health drinks and foods made by steeping fruit or grain in sugar, as in '매실 효소' (plum enzyme syrup). It often appears in compounds such as '소화 효소' (digestive enzyme).

examples.en: This company only makes high-quality products.
It's much clearer in high-quality video.
It's expensive, but I'm satisfied because it's high quality.
The taste is different because they use high-quality ingredients.
I saw an ad promising high-quality service.
Farmers work hard to grow high-quality rice.

explain: '고품질 제품', '고품질 서비스'처럼 뒤에 명사가 와요. 반대는 '저품질'이에요. 말할 때는 '품질이 좋다'가 더 자연스럽고, 고품질은 광고나 설명 글에 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: This shop is famous for its high-quality service.
phrases.nuance_ko: 광고나 설명 글에서 자주 보이는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing often seen in ads and descriptive writing.

phrases.en: The quality of these clothes is good.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때는 '고품질'보다 이 표현이 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: In speech, this sounds more natural than 'gopumjil'.

phrases.en: This restaurant uses only high-quality ingredients.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식이나 물건을 만드는 재료가 좋다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say the materials for food or products are good.

explain_en: A noun follows it: 고품질 제품, 고품질 서비스. The opposite is 저품질. In speech 품질이 좋다 sounds more natural; 고품질 mostly shows up in ads and descriptions.

en: to be straight; to be upright

examples.en: Please sit with your back straight.
If you follow the straight road, you will reach the school.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 마음이 곧발라서 거짓말을 못 해요.
examples.en: That child is so upright that he can't tell a lie.

examples.ko: 자세가 곧바르면 키도 더 커 보여요.
examples.en: If your posture is straight, you also look taller.

examples.ko: 곧발라 보이는 나무를 골라서 기둥으로 썼어요.
examples.en: We picked a tree that looked straight and used it as a pillar.
I promised my parents that I will live honestly from now on.

explain: 몸이나 물건이 굽지 않은 모습, 그리고 마음이 정직한 것에 모두 써요. '르' 불규칙이라 '곧발라요', '곧바른'으로 바뀌어요. 말할 때는 '곧게', '똑바로'처럼 말하는 사람이 많아요.

phrases.example: 곧바른 자세로 앉으면 허리가 덜 아파요.
phrases.en: If you sit with an upright posture, your back hurts less.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 쓰는 활용형이고 몸의 자세에 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used before nouns, often for body posture.

phrases.example: 사진 찍을 때 곧바르게 서 주세요.
phrases.en: Please stand up straight when taking the photo.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게'를 붙여서 어떻게 서는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-게', it describes how someone stands.

phrases.en: That person has an honest heart.
phrases.nuance_ko: '르' 불규칙 해요체이고 정직한 성격을 말할 수도 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The irregular polite form, and it can describe an honest character.

explain_en: It describes things that are not bent and also a person with an honest heart. It is a '르' irregular verb, so it becomes '곧발라요' and '곧바른'. In speech many people say '곧게' or '똑바로' instead.

t90.ax: Please sit with your back straight.

examples.ko: 힘든 일이 많았지만 그는 꿋꿋이 버텼어요.
examples.en: There was a lot of hardship, but he held out firmly.

examples.ko: 비바람 속에서도 나무가 꿋꿋이 서 있어요.
examples.en: The tree stands firm even in wind and rain.

examples.ko: 친구들이 놀려도 꿋꿋이 제 길을 갔어요.
examples.en: Even when friends teased him, he kept going his own way.
Grandmother keeps running the shop bravely, even on her own.
Even if you fail, try again with a strong heart.

examples.ko: 아이는 아파도 울지 않고 꿋꿋이 웃었어요.
examples.en: The child didn't cry even though it hurt, and smiled bravely.

explain: 어려운 일이 있어도 마음이 약해지지 않고 버티는 모습에 써요. 형용사 '꿋꿋하다'에서 나온 말이라 '꿋꿋한 사람'처럼도 말해요.

phrases.en: She lives on firmly even in hardship.
phrases.nuance_ko: '꿋꿋이'와 뜻이 같고, 일상에서 더 자주 들을 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '꿋꿋이', and you hear it more often in daily speech.

phrases.en: My grandmother is a really strong-minded person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 형용사 '꿋꿋하다'를 명사 앞에 써서 사람의 성격을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective '꿋꿋하다' before a noun describes a person's character.

phrases.en: I firmly endured the cold winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: '버티다'보다 '견디다'를 쓰면 힘든 시간을 참고 지나가는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '견디다', it feels like patiently getting through a hard time.

explain_en: It describes someone who stays strong and does not give in despite hardship. It comes from the adjective '꿋꿋하다', so you can also say '꿋꿋한 사람' (a resilient person).

t90.ax: The tree stands firm even in wind and rain.

examples.en: I solved the problem easily, so I felt good.
Thanks to the directions, I found the place easily.

examples.ko: 준비를 미리 하면 수월히 끝낼 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you prepare in advance, you can finish smoothly.
I thought it would be settled easily, but it wasn't.
I'm glad the child fell asleep without trouble.

examples.ko: 이 앱을 쓰면 수월히 예약할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you use this app, you can book easily.

explain: '수월하게'와 같은 뜻이고, 말할 때는 보통 '수월하게'나 '쉽게'를 더 많이 써요. '수월히'는 글에서 자연스러워요. 반대는 '힘들게'나 '어렵게'예요.

phrases.en: My friend helped, so the work finished easily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻이고 말할 때 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning and sounds more natural in speech.

phrases.example: 이 책은 쉽게 읽을 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can read this book easily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 가장 흔하게 쓰는 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common similar word in everyday conversation.

phrases.en: I finished my homework easily and went out to play.
phrases.nuance_ko: '끝내다', '해내다' 같은 동사와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with verbs like 끝내다 (finish) and 해내다 (accomplish).

explain_en: It means the same as '수월하게', and in speech people usually say '수월하게' or '쉽게' more. '수월히' sounds natural in writing. The opposite would be '힘들게' or '어렵게'.

t90.ax: If you use this app, you can book easily.

en: to be ordinary; to be normal; to be common

examples.en: This job is not just difficult, it's extremely difficult.
It's hard to pass with only an ordinary amount of effort.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 여간해서는 화를 내지 않아요.
examples.en: He hardly ever gets angry.

examples.ko: 아이를 혼자 키우는 게 여간 힘든 일이 아니에요.
examples.en: Raising a child alone is no easy thing at all.

examples.ko: 이렇게 도와주셔서 여간 고마운 게 아니에요.
examples.en: I can't tell you how grateful I am for your help.

examples.ko: 오늘은 여간 덥지 않아서 밖에 나가기 힘들어요.
examples.en: It's so hot today that it's hard to go outside.

explain: 거의 항상 부정 표현과 붙어 나와요. '여간 힘들지 않아요'는 모양은 부정인데 '무척 힘들어요'를 강하게 말해요. '여간해서는 화를 안 내요'처럼 쓰면 '웬만해서는'과 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I've been extremely busy lately.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모양은 부정이지만 '아주 ~하다'를 강하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Negative in form, but it strongly means 'very ~'.

phrases.en: That friend hardly ever cries.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 부정 표현이 와서 '쉽게는 ~않다'라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Followed by a negative to mean 'not easily'.

phrases.en: I almost never run late for appointments.
phrases.nuance_ko: '여간해서는'과 바꿔 쓸 수 있고, 일상 대화에서 더 흔해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Interchangeable with 여간해서는 and more common in daily conversation.
phrases.en_equiv: hardly ever; as a rule not

explain_en: It almost always comes with a negative. '여간 힘들지 않아요' looks negative but strongly means 'it's really hard'. In '여간해서는 화를 안 내요' it can be swapped with '웬만해서는' (hardly ever).

examples.en: The corner of this paper is a right angle.
The two lines meet at a right angle.
I placed the desk at a right angle to the wall.
I drew a right angle with a set square.

examples.ko: 길이 갑자기 직각으로 꺾여서 길을 잃었어요.
examples.en: The road turned sharply at a right angle, and I got lost.
Find the area of the right triangle.

explain: 90도가 직각이고, 90도보다 작으면 예각, 크면 둔각이에요. 길이나 선이 딱 꺾일 때도 '직각으로 꺾이다'라고 해요. 보통 '직각으로' 또는 '직각 삼각형'처럼 붙여서 써요.

phrases.en: I drew a right triangle in my notebook.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직각이 하나 있는 삼각형이고 수학 시간에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: A triangle with one right angle; common in math class.

phrases.en: This road bends at a right angle up ahead.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길이나 선이 딱 꺾이는 모양을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a road or line that turns sharply.

phrases.en: The two walls form a right angle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 면이나 선이 90도로 만날 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when two surfaces or lines meet at 90 degrees.

explain_en: 90 degrees is a right angle, smaller is '예각', and larger is '둔각'. A road or line that bends sharply can also '직각으로 꺾이다'. It usually appears as '직각으로' or '직각 삼각형'.

examples.en: He is a cultured person who reads a lot of books.
A cultured person should be quiet in public places.
I think universities should nurture well-rounded people.
She speaks in a way befitting a cultured person.

examples.ko: 그 작가는 폭넓은 지식을 가진 교양인으로 알려졌어요.
examples.en: The writer is known as a cultured person with broad knowledge.

examples.ko: 저도 사회에서 존중받는 교양인이 되고 싶어요.
examples.en: I also want to become a respected, cultured person in society.

explain: 지식이 많은 사람뿐 아니라 예의와 품위도 갖춘 사람이라는 느낌으로 쓰는 칭찬이나 기대의 말이에요. 같은 느낌으로 '교양 있는 사람'이라고도 많이 말해요.

phrases.example: 교양 있는 사람은 다른 사람의 말을 끝까지 들어요.
phrases.en: A refined person listens to others until the end.
phrases.nuance_ko: '교양인'과 같은 뜻이고, 일상 대화에서는 이 말을 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the same as 교양인, and is more common in everyday conversation.

phrases.en: Like a refined person, I speak quietly in the library.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-답다'를 붙여서 교양인에게 기대하는 모습대로 행동한다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -답다 says someone acts the way a refined person is expected to.
phrases.en_equiv: to act like a refined person

phrases.example: 책을 많이 읽고 교양인이 되고 싶어요.
phrases.en: I want to read a lot and become a refined person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교양인이 되고 싶다는 바람이나 목표를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about a wish or goal of becoming a refined person.

explain_en: It is a word of praise or expectation for someone who has not only knowledge but also manners and dignity. People also often say '교양 있는 사람' with the same feeling.

examples.ko: 이 팀은 구심점이 없어서 자꾸 흩어져요.
examples.en: This team has no central figure, so it keeps falling apart.

examples.ko: 그는 팀의 구심점 역할을 잘해 줬어요.
examples.en: He did a great job as the team's central pillar.
My grandmother is the center that holds our family together.

examples.ko: 새 대표가 조직의 구심점을 만들어야 해요.
examples.en: The new head has to create a rallying point for the organization.
The village hall served as a gathering point for the residents.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 팀의 구심점인 만큼 부담도 커요.
examples.en: As the team's focal point, that player also feels a lot of pressure.

explain: 사람들이 하나로 모이게 하는 중심이 되는 사람이나 곳을 말해요. 그냥 가운데라는 뜻의 '중심'과 달리, 흩어지지 않게 모아 주는 역할이 있어요. '구심점이 되다', '구심점을 잃다'처럼 자주 써요.

phrases.en: That player became the focal point of the team.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들이 모이는 중심 역할을 맡는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means taking the role of the center people gather around.

phrases.en: When the leader left, the group lost its center.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모이게 하던 중심이 없어져 흩어질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the unifying center disappears and people scatter.

phrases.example: 새 행사로 동네의 구심점을 만들고 싶어요.
phrases.en: I want to create a gathering point for the neighborhood with a new event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들을 모을 중심을 새로 세운다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means setting up a new center to bring people together.

explain_en: It refers to the person or place that serves as the center drawing people together. Unlike plain '중심' (center), it implies a role in keeping people from scattering. Common patterns are '구심점이 되다' and '구심점을 잃다'.

examples.ko: 동생은 눈썰미가 좋아서 한 번만 봐도 따라 해요.
examples.en: My younger sibling has a quick eye and copies things after seeing them just once.

examples.ko: 눈썰미 있는 직원이 새 일을 금방 배웠어요.
examples.en: The observant employee learned the new job quickly.

examples.ko: 저는 눈썰미가 없어서 길을 자주 잃어버려요.
examples.en: I'm not good at noticing things, so I often get lost.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 원래 눈썰미도 좋고 손끝도 야무져서 소문이 났어요.
examples.en: That friend has always been quick to learn and skilled with their hands, so word got around.

examples.ko: 할머니는 눈썰미가 대단해서 옷을 한 번 보면 똑같이 만드세요.
examples.en: My grandmother has a remarkable eye and can make a garment just like one she has seen once.
I relied only on watching and copying, and I made a mistake.

explain: '눈치'와 헷갈리기 쉬운데, 눈치는 분위기를 읽는 힘이고 눈썰미는 보고 따라 하는 솜씨예요. '눈썰미가 있다/좋다/없다'로 말하고, '손끝이 야무지다'와 함께 칭찬할 때도 나와요.

phrases.en: She has a good eye for learning, so she picks up cooking quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '눈썰미'에 '좋다'를 붙인 가장 흔한 칭찬 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to praise someone's knack for learning by watching.
phrases.en_equiv: to be quick at learning by watching

phrases.example: 눈썰미가 없어서 한 번 봐서는 따라 하지 못해요.
phrases.en: I'm not good at copying by watching, so I can't follow after seeing it once.
phrases.nuance_ko: 보고 따라 하는 솜씨가 부족하다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say someone is not good at picking things up by watching.
phrases.en_equiv: to lack a knack for learning by watching

phrases.example: 눈썰미 있는 사람은 일을 빨리 배워요.
phrases.en: People who learn quickly by watching pick up work fast.
phrases.nuance_ko: '있는'을 붙여 사람을 꾸며 주는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses 있는 to describe a person with this skill.
phrases.en_equiv: a person who learns quickly by watching

explain_en: It is easy to mix up with '눈치' (reading the mood): 눈치 is about sensing the atmosphere, while 눈썰미 is the knack of picking things up by watching. You say '눈썰미가 있다/좋다/없다', and it sometimes appears together with '손끝이 야무지다' when praising someone.

en: easy and fluent speaking; being glib

examples.ko: 그 사람은 달변이라서 발표를 정말 잘해요.
examples.en: He is such a fluent speaker that he gives really good presentations.
He moved people's hearts with his eloquent speech.
I'm not a smooth talker, but I'll speak sincerely.

examples.ko: 면접에서는 달변보다 솔직함이 더 중요할 때도 있어요.
examples.en: In interviews, honesty is sometimes more important than eloquence.

examples.ko: 친구는 말솜씨가 좋아서 달변이라는 말을 자주 들어요.
examples.en: My friend is good with words, so people often call him eloquent.

examples.ko: 영업 사원이라고 다 달변인 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Not every salesperson is a smooth talker.

explain: '말을 잘하다', '말솜씨가 좋다'가 일상에서는 더 자연스럽고, 달변은 좀 격식 있는 말이에요. 반대말은 '눌변'이고, 사람을 가리킬 때는 '달변가'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: He is a person everyone recognizes as an eloquent speaker.
phrases.nuance_ko: 달변이 말솜씨라면 달변가는 말을 잘하는 사람을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: While 달변 is the skill, 달변가 refers to the person who speaks fluently.

phrases.en: The host was eloquent, so the mood was good.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 말을 잘한다는 것을 '이다'를 붙여 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '이다' to describe a person as a fluent speaker.

phrases.en: My younger sibling speaks really well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 달변보다 일상에서 훨씬 자연스럽고 편하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A much more natural, everyday way to say the same thing as 달변.

explain_en: In daily talk '말을 잘하다' or '말솜씨가 좋다' sounds more natural, and 달변 is somewhat formal. Its opposite is '눌변', and for a person you can also say '달변가'.

examples.en: A senior who had returned to school helped me with the class.
I'll be a returning student next year too.
There are many returning students in our department.
Since I'm a returning student, I'm older than the freshmen.
Let's go to the returning students' gathering together.
I asked a returning student how to register for classes.

explain: 휴학했다가 다시 학교에 돌아온 대학생을 말해요. 보통 군대에 다녀온 남학생을 떠올리는 경우가 많고, 새로 입학한 '새내기'와 대비해서 나이가 더 많은 선배라는 느낌이 있어요. 반대로 학교를 쉬는 학생은 '휴학생'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I'm going to return to school next semester.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학생이 학교로 돌아오는 행동을 말하는 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb for a student returning to school.

phrases.example: 복학생 선배가 시험 공부 방법을 알려 줬어요.
phrases.en: A senior who just came back from leave taught me how to study for exams.
phrases.nuance_ko: 군대나 휴학을 마치고 돌아온 선배를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A senior who has come back after military service or leave.

phrases.example: 복학 신청은 이번 주까지 해야 해요.
phrases.en: You have to apply to return to school by this week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교에 돌아오려고 서류를 내는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to submitting paperwork to return to school.

explain_en: It means a university student who has come back after taking time off. People often picture a male student back from military service, and the word contrasts with '새내기' (freshman) with a feeling of an older senior. A student on leave is a '휴학생'.
